sentences.text: 2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri S.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent - State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the record.

3. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioners are brothers and their father Mohammed Yousuf had a shop in Ajmer, Rajasthan dealing with artificial jewellery and American diamonds.

It is further contended that respondent No.2 approached the father of the petitioners by introducing himself as an admirer of American diamonds and that he runs Islamic institutions around the world and collects donations in the name of the same and also expressed his desire to open such institution in India.

During his visit to India, respondent No.2 came to Hyderabad and at that time the mother of the petitioner purchased a land for construction of house admeasuring 400 Sq. Yds. in Plot Nos.102 and 105 in Sy.Nos.187 (Part) and 191, 193 and 194 situated at Bandlaguda Khalsa, Rajendra Nagar, Ranga Reddy District, through a registered sale deed vide document No.1971 of 2011 dated 09.06.2011 by selling other lands in her name and her gold jewellery.
Respondent No.2 visited the petitioners for the second time in Hyderabad, at that time, the construction of their house had begun and a contractor was also engaged.

After coming and seeing the construction, respondent No.2 conveyed his wish of establishing an Islamic institution in the land of the petitioners and that could collect donation but the same was denied by the parents of the petitioners.
In spite of it, respondent No.2 pestered the parents of the petitioners and also started spreading false rumors that the petitioners are constructing Islamic institution in their land.
In the year 2013, with the assistance of Police personnel, respondent No.2 started harassing the petitioners and their parents.

It is stated that petitioner No.2 was summoned by the police on several occasions and due to unbearable torture made by the police, the mother of the petitioners approached the State Human Right Commission vide H.R. Case No.5774/2013 and thereafter petitioner No.2 was released.

It is also contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that a private complaint was filed by respondent No.2 and the same was registered as F.I.R. No.657 of 2019 on the file of the Station House Offiecer, Mailardevapally Police Station, Ranga Reddy District, registered for the above said offences.

entities.text: Mailardevapally Police Station, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The police issued notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. to the petitioners herein.

It is further contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the incident as to the construction and pestering the petitioners took place in the year 2013; the father of the petitioners died in the year 2016; false FIR has been registered in the year 2019 and therefore, it is a fit case to quash all the proceedings against the petitioners.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor contended that as the charge sheet is already filed and C.C. is numbered and it is coming up for trial in the Court below.
Therefore, it is not a fit case to quash the proceedings against the petitioner at this juncture.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that respondent No.2 also filed vacate stay petition in the present case and in view of the stay granted by this Court, the trial could not be proceeded with.

It is the specific contention of respondent No.2 that he gave hard earned money for construction of religious school keeping in view the financial difficulties of poor and needy students of the Hyderabad city, but due to greedy nature of the petitioners and their father,
the entire amounts kept for a welfare purpose was swindled by them.
Therefore, the crime registered against the petitioners is maintainable.

6. Taking into consideration that the matter is to be decided only after conducting the trial, this Court is of the considered view that trial Court shall proceeded with the trial in C.C.No.2503 of 2022.

Further, the trial Court is directed to dispose of the calendar case within a period of six (06)
months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

In the meanwhile, the appearance/attendance of the petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 in C.C.No.2563 of 2022 pending on the file of learned XII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate at Cyberabad, Rajendranagar, Ranga Reddy District, is dispensed with, unless their presence is required by the trial Court for a specific purpose or at the time of recording their examination under Section 313 Cr.P.C. and on the date of pronouncement of judgment.

entities.text: XII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate at Cyberabad, Rajendranagar, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: No such relief is given so far as petitioner/accused No.3 is concerned.

Further, the petitioners are at liberty to file an application seeking discharge and on such application being filed,
the trial Court shall dispose of the same on merits without getting influenced by the observations made by this Court in the present order.
7.
With the above observation, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
